description.summary: the screens that are plugged in, and how they are set

protocol.description:
How Display settings, the start-up scale and About this computer learn which screens there are, what each can do and how each is set, and how they change the arrangement.
A program is first told about every screen, then, whenever anything changes, about the screens that changed. Each batch ends with "settled", which carries a serial number. To change the arrangement a program makes a plan quoting the latest serial, describes every screen in it, and applies it. If the screens changed in between, the plan is turned away as stale, so a change is never made from an out-of-date picture.
A plan is applied whole or not at all. Offered only to programs the compositor trusts with the screens.

description.summary: where the screens are asked about

request.name: destroy

description.summary: no more news of the screens is wanted

request.description: Screens and plans already made are not affected.

request.name: plan

description.summary: start a new arrangement

request.description: Nothing changes until the plan is applied.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: the serial of the last settled event the plan was made from

event.name: screen

description.summary: a screen is plugged in

event.description: Its description follows on the screen, and the batch ends with "settled".

event.name: settled

description.summary: everything sent so far is complete

event.description: The serial goes up whenever any screen changes.

interface.name: trindle_screen_v1

description.summary: one screen

interface.description: A change to a screen arrives as "clear" followed by its whole description again, so a program replaces what it knew rather than patching it.

enum.name: turn

description.summary: which way up the picture is drawn

enum.description: The numbers are the ones wl_output uses for its transform.

entry.name: quarter
entry.summary: turned a quarter, to the left

entry.name: preferred
entry.summary: the size and rate the screen asks for

description.summary: forget this screen

event.name: clear

description.summary: what was said about this screen no longer holds

event.description: A new description follows: identity, size_mm, one mode for each way it can be driven and then layout.

event.name: identity

description.summary: what the screen is

event.description: The name is the connector, such as HDMI-A-1, the same one wl_output gives. Words that are not known are empty.

arg.name: description
arg.summary: maker, model and connector in words

event.name: size_mm

description.summary: how big the screen is

event.description: Millimetres across and down. Both are 0 when the screen does not say.

event.name: mode

description.summary: one way the screen can be driven

event.description: Sent once for each, in the order the screen lists them; the first is number 0. A refresh of 0 means the rate is not known.

arg.name: millihertz
arg.summary: pictures a second in thousandths: 60 Hz is 60000

event.name: layout

description.summary: how the screen is set now

event.description: The position is that of its top-left corner in the layout, counted in the layout's own units (real pixels divided by the scale).

arg.name: on
arg.summary: 1 if it is lit, 0 if it is switched off

arg.name: mode
arg.summary: the number of the mode in use, or 4294967295 when off

arg.name: turn
arg.summary: which way up, as the turn enum numbers it

arg.name: varies_rate
arg.summary: 1 if it varies its refresh rate to suit the picture

event.name: unplugged

description.summary: the screen has gone

event.description: Nothing more is sent for it. The program should destroy the object.

interface.name: trindle_screen_plan_v1

description.summary: a new arrangement of the screens

interface.description: Describe every screen that is plugged in with "screen", then "apply" (or "check" to ask without changing anything). A screen left out, or named twice, or a plan that would leave every screen off, is refused.

entry.name: refused
entry.summary: the arrangement cannot be used; the words say why

entry.name: stale
entry.summary: the screens changed since the plan's serial; look again

request.name: destroy

description.summary: finish with this plan

request.description: Whether or not it was applied.

request.name: screen

description.summary: say how one screen should be

request.description: If it is to be off, the rest is ignored. If a size is given (width and height above 0) the screen is switched on at the listed mode of that size and the nearest rate within a hertz of the one asked for; a rate of 0 means the one the screen prefers, else the fastest. A size of 0 keeps the mode in use now, or the preferred one for a screen that was off. The scale is in 120ths and is kept to between a quarter and ten.

arg.name: on
arg.summary: 1 to light it, 0 to switch it off

arg.name: millihertz
arg.summary: pictures a second in thousandths, or 0

arg.name: turn
arg.summary: which way up, as the turn enum of trindle_screen_v1 numbers it

request.name: apply

description.summary: make the arrangement

request.description: Answered by "outcome". A plan can be applied once.

description.summary: ask whether the arrangement would be accepted
how the plan went

arg.name: why
arg.summary: a few words saying why, empty if it was applied
